paper.title: Grassmann Variational Monte Carlo with neural wave functions
paper.authors: Douglas Hendry, Alessandro Sinibaldi, Giuseppe Carleo

results.system_description: Heisenberg, 10 × 10 · J = 1 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift
results.method: Grassmann VMC, ConvNeXt CNN backflow with RBM heads
results.variant: ground state |E_0> of a 6-state jointly optimized subspace, sector (q_x, q_y, q_sf) = (0, 0, 0)
results.eligibility_evidence: Directly evaluated VMC energy of the authors' own neural wave functions (a CNN backflow with RBM heads), the ground state of a jointly optimized multi-state model; not an extrapolation, projector estimate or quoted value.
results.notes: Printed V-score 1e-4; the paper's QMC reference for this state is shown in Fig. 10x10. The ansatz is the span of several neural wave functions phi_i(s) = f_theta_i(CNN_Theta(s)): a shared real-valued ConvNeXt-style CNN acting as a common backflow of the spin configuration, followed by one complex-valued RBM head per state, with the Marshall sign rule applied, translation and spin-flip symmetry enforced, and sampling restricted to zero total S^z (Sec. on the Heisenberg model). The states are optimized jointly with Grassmann VMC, and the printed E_0 is the lowest eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian projected on the optimized subspace, a Ritz upper bound on the ground-state energy. Ground states of jointly optimized multi-state models are eligible by the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-26. The (q_x, q_y, q_sf) = (0, 0, 0) sector holds the ground state for this even-L lattice (Marshall sign, N/2 even). The paper does not state the meaning of the parenthesized error, so it is recorded as unspecified.
